summary: A 1950 Forest Service-type cab on a nine-foot enclosed tower, burned in 1951 and reconstructed, on private timber land on Green Mountain, Linn County, Oregon; standing and unstaffed.

facts.design: Standard 14x14 Forest Service-type cab on a 9 ft enclosed tower (labelled L-4 by firelookout.com, BC-301 by the register)

access.note: Private timber land behind a closed locked gate. A gate sign allows non-motorized recreation access when the industrial fire precaution level is at 1 or lower (2026 visit). The register lists the site as private land.

events.note: Site first established as a camp, per firelookout.com
Completed August 22, 1950 by Knight and a crew of three men; register credits Santiam Lumber Company with the build
June 21, 1951: the Fire Patrol lookout station on Green Mountain burned to the ground; sparks from the cookstove started the blaze; a two-way radio and a fire-finder were lost
Reconstructed in 1951 after the fire, per Every Lookout in Oregon
Used for emergencies in the 1970s, per firelookout.com (decade only)
Surveyed at private owners' request to estimate restoration cost and whether the FFLA Oregon Chapter would adopt it; second trip sealed the cab for winter
2020 Holiday Farm Fire burned trees on the slopes of the mountain; the lookout came close to being destroyed but survived
Registered June 22, 2022 as US 1607, OR 134; nominated by Brad Eells

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on the builder (register: Santiam Lumber Company; the August 1950 item quoted by Forest Lookouts: Fire Patrol crew) and on distance from Sweet Home (32 miles in the August 1950 item, 16 miles on firelookout.com); the story reports both without choosing. The record's '2007 restored' looks wrong and is proposed as a correction; the 2007 report describes a survey and winter sealing only. Design labels differ (BC-301, L-4, 14x14 type). The original cab burned to the ground on June 21, 1951 (Albany Democrat-Herald, quoted by Forest Lookouts); Every Lookout in Oregon says it was reconstructed in 1951. The sources do not say how much of the standing cab is the 1951 rebuild, so the 1950 build date may not describe the structure visitors see today. An earlier note that no notable fire appears in the sources was wrong. The 2020 Holiday Farm Fire came close; the lookout survived. Access: private timber land behind a closed locked gate; a gate sign allows non-motorized recreation at fire precaution level 1 or lower. The 2026 description is a single blog visit.
